claims.claim: Cheniere sits on a durable gas-to-LNG-to-global-energy bridge: liquefaction infrastructure converts North American feedgas into dispatchable traded energy, but resilience depends on feedgas availability, terminal uptime, contracted demand and disciplined expansion economics.
The principal successor bottlenecks are feedgas/pipeline capacity, liquefaction reliability, shipping/regasification access and permitting/capex rather than liquefaction technology alone.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Large operating liquefaction infrastructure and completed Stage 3 capacity create hard-to-replicate physical conversion capacity.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Contracted LNG infrastructure can remain useful across gas-price scenarios, while utilization and expansion returns remain exposed to spreads, feedgas and regulation.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: LNG serves dispatchable energy and industrial demand but competes over time with domestic gas use, renewables-plus-storage, nuclear and other supply routes.

causalEdges.mechanism: pipeline feedgas is converted into exportable LNG
LNG cargoes bridge geographically separated gas supply and demand
physical export capacity plus contracted offtake can diversify supply, subject to uptime and shipping access

risks.risk: Successor bottlenecks can migrate from liquefaction construction to feedgas, shipping/regasification, permitting and financing discipline.

unknowns.unknown: Long-run realized returns on pending expansions and future LNG spreads remain uncertain.

claims.claim: The operating thesis is not falsified by GAAP net-loss volatility alone; derivative/accounting effects must be separated from physical throughput and cash economics.

Leverage and capital intensity remain material resilience constraints: Cheniere reported roughly $23B of debt at year-end 2025, so expansion value depends on contract quality, utilization and refinancing/capital discipline.

factors.name: financingResilience
factors.basis: Large fixed infrastructure supports cash generation but substantial debt and future expansion capex reduce error tolerance.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Raised guidance and completed trains should not be extrapolated into guaranteed future expansion returns.

risks.risk: Debt/capex intensity, terminal outages, feedgas constraints, permitting changes and weaker contract/spread economics can impair expansion returns.

contradictions.claim: GAAP loss versus strong adjusted EBITDA
contradictions.resolution: Treat as an accounting/economic reconciliation issue rather than evidence that physical operations failed; Deep Resolver retains contradiction disposition authority.

unknowns.unknown: Incremental expansion financing mix and realized project returns are not yet known.
